newsitem.title: USA: R.R. Donnelley probes offensive e-mail.
newsitem.headline: R.R. Donnelley probes offensive e-mail.

text.p: R.R. Donnelley & Sons Co, named in a racial discrimination suit in December, said Friday it was investigating the source of offensive electronic mail that plaintiffs allege circulated through its system.
William Lowe, a spokesman for the printer, said his company received documents listing 165 racial, ethnic and sexual jokes said to be created at a Donnelley plant in Lancaster, Pa.
"We haven't confirmed it, but it looks to be a Donnelley document," Lowe told Reuters. "The question is when, how, by whom and where was this created and how was it distributed."

In a statement, Jonathan Ward, R.R. Donnelley executive vice president and president-commercial print sector, said, "We have zero tolerance for discrimination, and this act is a clear violation of our explicit company policy and values."

The $500 million class-action lawsuit charges that R.R. Donnelley discriminated against black employees when arranging transfers to other jobs in 1993 related to a plant closing. The company has denied the charges. No date has been set for a hearing.
Donnelley said its minority employment level totals about 13 percent. It said jobs held by African-Americans advanced seven percent between 1995 and 1996.
